stories.title: Human intestinal epithelium reveals divergent Salmonella cell tropism
stories.takeaway: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella lineages show differing preferences for human intestinal epithelial cell targets.
stories.what_happened: Researchers compared intestinal epithelial interactions of Salmonella lineages with distinct host ranges, identifying divergence in cell tropism.
stories.why_it_matters: Human-relevant intestinal infection models can help test pathogen specificity beyond conventional animal-host assumptions.
stories.caveat: Cell tropism in experimental epithelial systems does not alone establish clinical severity or transmission differences.

stories.title: Placenta-on-a-chip reveals sublethal functional injury from cadmium
stories.takeaway: A human placental microphysiological model detected impaired nutrient transport, hormone secretion and barrier function at exposures that did not cause overt cell death.
stories.what_happened: A perfused maternal–fetal interface chip incorporating human placental cells and vascularized tissue was challenged with cadmium; researchers measured transport, permeability, metabolism and protective BCRP activity.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates why human organ-chip safety studies need functional endpoints in addition to cell viability.
stories.caveat: Preclinical chip results and candidate metabolic biomarkers require independent validation in pregnancy cohorts.

stories.title: Colorectal cancer review examines stem-cell niches and tumor heterogeneity
stories.takeaway: A new synthesis frames colorectal tumor initiation around stem-cell competition, crypt niche constraints and ectopic stem-cell states.
stories.what_happened: The review integrates evidence on intestinal crypt organization, cellular origins and regional heterogeneity in colorectal cancer.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides a conceptual framework for evaluating cell-state plasticity and niche context in human intestinal disease models.
stories.caveat: This is a review synthesizing diverse systems, not a single prospective experimental demonstration.

stories.title: Gut microbial glycine lipids linked to mitochondrial metabolism in mice
stories.takeaway: Bacteroidota-derived glycine lipids were associated with improved liver or muscle mitochondrial responses in separate mouse studies.
stories.what_happened: Investigators studied microbiome-derived lipid metabolites in diet-associated mouse models, including liver steatosis and skeletal muscle bioenergetics.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how microbial metabolites can influence host physiology outside the intestine and motivate mechanistic host–microbe studies.
stories.caveat: Animal models and specific lipid exposures do not establish therapeutic benefits in humans.

stories.title: Microbial proline dipeptides illuminate rumen nitrogen efficiency
stories.takeaway: New work identifies rumen-microbe-derived proline-containing peptides associated with more efficient nitrogen utilization in dairy cattle.
stories.what_happened: Researchers investigated microbial peptide production and its contribution to ruminant nitrogen metabolism.
stories.why_it_matters: Highlights metabolite-resolved microbiome function and translational applications in sustainable biotechnology.
stories.caveat: Ruminant digestive physiology differs substantially from the human gut; human-health implications are speculative.
